facts.t: The phrase judicial review appears nowhere in the Constitution
facts.d: Article 13 renders inconsistent laws void, Articles 32 and 226 supply writ remedies, but the power itself is never named. L. Chandra Kumar nonetheless declared Articles 32 and 226 part of the basic structure — an unnamed power made unamendable.

facts.t: Only the Supreme Court can revisit its own final judgment
facts.d: Review petitions under Article 137 and curative petitions under the Rupa Ashok Hurra guidelines exist nowhere else in the Indian system. A High Court cannot cure its own final decision the way the Supreme Court can.

facts.t: Delimitation orders cannot be challenged in any court
facts.d: Articles 329, 243-O and 243-ZG expressly bar judicial interference with delimitation and electoral roll matters. It is one of the few areas where the Constitution itself shuts the courtroom door.

bank.q: Articles 32 and 226 were declared part of the basic structure in:
bank.e: L. Chandra Kumar (1997), which also held that tribunals may supplement but never supplant constitutional courts.

bank.q: With reference to the powers of the Supreme Court and High Courts, consider the following:
s: Only the Supreme Court may entertain review petitions under Article 137.
Curative petitions arise from the guidelines in Rupa Ashok Hurra.
High Courts and the Supreme Court have identical powers of judicial review.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Their powers are not identical — Articles 131, 142 and 143 belong to the Supreme Court alone.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT expressly excluded from judicial review?
o: Advice tendered by the Council of Ministers to the President
Ninth Schedule laws added after 24 April 1973
bank.e: I. R. Coelho held that post-1973 Ninth Schedule entries are reviewable against fundamental rights and the basic structure. The other three are expressly excluded.

bank.q: Match List I (article) with List II (jurisdiction):
pairs: 4. High Court transfer of specific cases
bank.e: Article 131 for federal disputes, 142 for complete justice, 143 for presidential references, and 228 for High Court transfers.

bank.as: Courts avoid ruling on the wisdom of policy decisions.
bank.rs: The political question doctrine and the presumption of constitutionality place the burden on the challenger.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — self-restraint reinforced by deference to the expertise of specialised bodies.

bank.q: Consider the following as negative impacts attributed to judicial review:
s: A democratic deficit exposed by the NJAC judgment.
Delayed reform, as with the stay on the farm laws.
Protection of minorities in Navtej Singh Johar.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are listed among the negatives. Navtej Singh Johar appears among the positive impacts.

bank.q: All of the following are doctrines that enhance judicial review EXCEPT:
bank.e: Sovereign immunity limits liability rather than enhancing review. The others, along with eclipse, severability and harmonious construction, expand the reviewing court's toolkit.

bank.q: Which immunity protects the President and Governors from suit for official acts?
bank.e: Article 361. Article 218 read with Article 124(4) supplies the parallel protection for judges.

bank.q: With reference to procedural constraints on judicial review, consider the following:
s: Locus standi remains a threshold requirement, though liberalised by public interest litigation.
Res judicata bars re-litigation of settled matters.
There are no limitation periods for writ petitions.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Time limitations do apply — delay and laches can defeat a writ petition.

bank.q: Which case is cited as an instance of judicial self-restraint?
bank.e: Supriyo, the same-sex marriage case, where the Court declined to legislate and left the question to Parliament.

bank.as: Judicial review is described as sine qua non for Indian democracy.
bank.rs: India combines a written constitution, a federal structure and one of the world's most extensive rights guarantees.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — each of those features requires an umpire, and judicial review supplies it.
